text:
maria: Heads up — found a staging repro where proxied requests are being charged to the proxy project instead of the originating project. Noticed during a quota spike overnight.
chris: I saw that too. Traces show the header with origin gets dropped during the exchange step: `proxy -> auth-exchange -> runtime`.
anne: We intentionally strip untrusted headers in auth-exchange to prevent spoofing. If we accept an origin claim we need an attestation method, not just a header.
tj: Quick proposal: have auth-exchange mint a short-lived, signed attestation token containing `origin_project` and `origin_request_id`. Pass that as `X-Redwood-Origin: <attestation_jwt>` from proxy to runtime. Runtime validates signature via auth-exchange introspect.
samir: Security concern: who can request that attestation? If any proxy can ask, they could claim billing for other orgs. We'll need a policy that only services with `impersonate:origin` scope and explicit allowlist can get attestation for a different project.
maria: Agreed. Minimal implementation: auth-exchange issues an attestation JWT only when the caller is authorized and we record the decision in the audit log. Example header we discussed:
```
X-Redwood-Origin: v1.jwt eyJhbGci... (claims: {"origin_project":"proj:alice/42","issued_by":"auth-exchange","exp":1680000000})
```
chris: Also we must change billing & telemetry: log three fields on each request span — `ingress_project` (where token came from), `origin_project` (attested by JWT), and `charged_project` (what we actually billed). Make cost events include all three so we can reconcile.
anne: Console UX idea: in the usage dashboards add a toggle to view usage by `charged_project` or by `origin_project`. For proxied traffic show a "proxied" badge and let owners drill into the attestation token and audit log. Also surface anomalies: sudden increases in `origin_project` traffic that doesn't match typical patterns.
tj: Rollout plan suggestion: (1) enable debug telemetry in staging to collect both origin and charged fields for 2 weeks with no billing change, (2) run reconciliation jobs to validate heuristics, (3) enable billing for a small canary (10% of orgs) with opt-out, (4) expand. Default fallback remains: if no valid attestation, charge to the proxy.
samir: Edge cases: cross-project background jobs (cron, data pipelines) intentionally forward requests. We need an allowlist + a reconciliation API to do periodic transfers or refunds when needed. Also think about quotas — if origin_project is billed, quotas must decrement against origin's quota unless policy forbids.
maria: I'll own the auth-exchange work (attestation minting + audit logs). Need someone on runtime/telemetry and someone for console changes.
chris: I'll pick up runtime + telemetry traces. I'll add the `charged_project` field to cost events and a flag to validate JWTs at ingress. I'll open a tiny RFC and a tracking ticket.
anne: I'll mock console wireframes for the new drill-down and anomaly alerts. Will also propose the UX for opt-out during canary.
tj: For the policy layer, I'll draft the allowlist + scope model and a few example policies for common patterns (proxy-for-tenant, cross-project-pipelines).
samir: Let's remember to add tests for abuse cases: replayed attestation, forged headers, and stale JWTs. Also we should simulate spike scenarios to make sure quota math doesn't explode.
maria: Who wants to be the owner to land the first PR to auth-exchange? I can start a branch today.
chris: I can start the runtime PR tomorrow. I'll instrument telemetry first (no billing change) so we can validate.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: RFC created: https://go/internal/rfcs/RED-3123 — "attested-origin-affinity". Owners: maria, chris, anne, tj. Added tracking ticket RED-4120. :white_check_mark:
